item.title: [LU-20363] Ubuntu 26.04 sanity test_33i: FAIL: ls list 728 files, 245 files on MDT1
item.description:
This issue was created by maloo for jianyu <yujian@whamcloud.com>

This issue relates to the following test suite run: https://testing.whamcloud.com/test_sets/8a41beb2-30b7-426c-977f-14838bcb9e63

status.description: A resolution has been taken, and it is awaiting verification by reporter. From here issues are either reopened, or are closed.

comments.comment:
Still using strace to grasp the syscall log.

On Rocky 9 client, the ls command in sanity test_33i will act like this:

openat(AT_FDCWD, "/mnt/lustre/d33i.sanity", O_RDONLY|O_NONBLOCK|O_CLOEXEC|O_DIRECTORY) = 3
fstat(3, {st_mode=S_IFDIR|0755, st_size=421888, ...}) = 0
mmap(NULL, 1052672, PROT_READ|PROT_WRITE, MAP_PRIVATE|MAP_ANONYMOUS, -1, 0) = 0x7fad232ff000
getdents64(3, 0x7fad232ff040 /* 510 entries */, 1048576) = 141912
brk(0x5569f8c33000)                     = 0x5569f8c33000
mmap(NULL, 163840, PROT_READ|PROT_WRITE, MAP_PRIVATE|MAP_ANONYMOUS, -1, 0) = 0x7fad30c65000
getdents64(3, 0x7fad232ff040 /* 0 entries */, 1048576) = 0
munmap(0x7fad232ff000, 1052672)         = 0
close(3)                                = -1 ESHUTDOWN 
...

and return ESHUTDOWN.

But on a Ubuntu 26.04 client, the ls command in sanity test_33i

munmap(0x7cce6dce5000, 155648)          = 0
munmap(0x7cce6d8ff000, 1052672)         = 0
close(3)                                = -1 ESHUTDOWN (Cannot send after transport endpoint shutdown)
gettid()                                = 99304
write(2, "\nthread 'main' (99304) panicked "..., 203
thread 'main' (99304) panicked at library/std/src/sys/fs/unix.rs:887:9:
unexpected error during closedir: Os { code: 108, kind: Uncategorized, message: "Cannot send after transport endpoint shutdown" }
) = 203
write(2, "note: run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1"..., 78note: run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace
) = 78
gettid()                                = 99304
getpid()                                = 99304
tgkill(99304, 99304, SIGABRT)           = 0
--- SIGABRT {si_signo=SIGABRT, si_code=SI_TKILL, si_pid=99304, si_uid=0} ---
+++ killed by SIGABRT (core dumped) +++

The process will abort.

With "library/std/src/sys/fs/unix.rs" and  "RUST_BACKTRACE" in the log, the ls on Ubuntu 26.04 doesn't seems like a traditional GNU ls command.

root@wangxiyang-ubuntu26:~# ls -l /usr/bin/ls /usr/bin/gnuls
-rwxr-xr-x 1 root root 150568 Jan 23 21:41 /usr/bin/gnuls
lrwxrwxrwx 1 root root     29 Mar 31 00:50 /usr/bin/ls -> ../lib/cargo/bin/coreutils/ls

A simple way to solve this problem is to make /usr/bin/ls point to gnuls before the test.

Or we will have to use gnuls in the test script to avoid this problem.

"Xiyang Wang <xiwang@ddn.com>" uploaded a new patch: https://review.whamcloud.com/c/fs/lustre-release/+/66726
Subject: LU-20363 tests: use GNU ls in sanity test_33i
Project: fs/lustre-release
Branch: master
Current Patch Set: 1
Commit: 917748062bb78e13558fc1c2bc421a01bee8adb8
You should report the bug in the rust 'ls' to upstream https://github.com/uutils/coreutils if you haven't already.

After DCO-11530 (ubuntu26 tests VMs should use coreutils-from-gnu) was resolved, sanity test 33i passed:
https://testing.whamcloud.com/test_sets/8ee4542c-f4a9-4996-95fe-20892f3c11dc
https://testing.whamcloud.com/test_sets/88069434-45dd-4b38-a1cf-2f1d744bd519
Let's close this ticket.
